nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable if for every orientation $D$ of $G$ there is a map $c \colon V \to \{0, \dots, k - 1\}$, not required to be a proper colouring, such that no closed directed walk of positive length in $D$ has all of its vertices of the same colour under $c$.
nodes.title: Dichromatically $k$-colourable graphs

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. If $G$ is dichromatically $n$-colourable for some natural number $n$, then the dichromatic number of $G$ equals the least natural number $k$ such that $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable.
nodes.title: The dichromatic number as a least natural number

nodes.summary: The dichromatic number of a simple graph $G$ is the least natural number $k$ such that $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$; it is $\infty$ if $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable for no natural number $k$.
nodes.title: Dichromatic number

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be a binary relation on a set $V$, viewed as a digraph, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f_0, f_1, \dots, f_{n+1}$ be elements of $V$. The sequence $(f_0, \dots, f_{n+1})$ is a closed directed walk of length $n + 1$ in $D$ if $f_0 = f_{n+1}$ and $D(f_i, f_{i+1})$ holds for every $i$ with $0 \le i \le n$.
nodes.title: Closed directed walks

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$. A binary relation $D$ on $V$ is an orientation of $G$ if $D(u, v)$ holds only when $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$, and for every pair of adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$ exactly one of $D(u, v)$ and $D(v, u)$ holds.
nodes.title: Orientations of a graph

nodes.summary: If a simple graph $G$ has no edges, then $G$ is dichromatically $1$-colourable.
nodes.title: Edgeless graphs are dichromatically $1$-colourable

nodes.summary: If a simple graph $G$ has no edges, then the empty relation on its vertex set, the digraph with no arcs, is an orientation of $G$.
nodes.title: The empty orientation of an edgeless graph

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
